title: Critical WordPress Flaw Exposed 500 Million Sites to Remote Takeover
excerpt: A vulnerability chain dubbed XSS2Shell allows attackers to achieve full remote code execution on WordPress servers through a single failed login attempt, with no authentication required.
body:
• CVE-2026-64638, nicknamed XSS2Shell, is a pre-authentication vulnerability chain that turns a failed WordPress login attempt into full remote code execution
  • The flaw has existed since WordPress 4.7 and affected every actively maintained installation — an estimated 500 million+ websites, or 43% of all internet-facing sites
  • WordPress shipped an emergency patch in version 7.0.3 on August 6, 2026, with fixes backported to every maintained branch back to WordPress 4.7
  • No active exploitation has been confirmed so far, but site administrators running self-hosted WordPress should update immediately

A Parser Disagreement at the Core

Security researchers at pwn.ai have disclosed a critical vulnerability chain in WordPress Core that allows an unauthenticated attacker to escalate from a single failed login attempt to full remote code execution on the underlying server. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-64638 and nicknamed XSS2Shell, has been present in WordPress since version 4.7 — effectively since some of the earliest versions of the platform.

The attack exploits a disagreement between two of WordPress's own text sanitization systems. When a non-existent username is submitted on the login page, WordPress builds an error message using a function called wp_strip_all_tags, which wraps PHP's strip_tags. PHP's parser identifies HTML tags by looking for an opening angle bracket immediately followed by a letter. Inserting a space between the bracket and the tag name — such as < area — causes PHP to treat it as harmless text.

But WordPress's own KSES sanitizer, which processes the string downstream, handles that whitespace differently. To KSES, < area is a valid <area> element — and <area> is on the WordPress allowlist. The result: attacker-controlled HTML elements are smuggled directly into the rendered login page with no account or prior authentication required.

From XSS to Shell Access

The injected elements alone do not execute scripts. But the researchers found that WordPress loads a JavaScript file called user-profile.js on the login page — a script originally written for the profile editing page that remains loaded because the login page also handles password resets. This script automatically searches for specific CSS selectors and triggers click events on matching elements.

Through a technique called DOM clobbering, the attacker's injected elements hijack the destination URL of an automatically triggered AJAX request, redirecting it to WordPress's REST API with JSONP parameters. The response returns as executable JavaScript, which jQuery's globalEval() executes in the WordPress origin.

"The vulnerability has been present since the earliest versions of WordPress and was somehow missed by every audit until now. It affects pretty much all WordPress sites that are still supported. If you run WordPress, update now."

— pwn.ai Security Research

Full Server Compromise in Five Steps

The pre-authentication XSS alone is serious, but the researchers demonstrated a complete chain to PHP remote code execution. If a logged-in administrator visits a malicious page, the attacker's script can piggyback on the admin's session to mint a WordPress Application Password, publish a page containing attacker JavaScript using the admin's unfiltered HTML privileges, and upload a malicious plugin ZIP containing a PHP web shell — all through legitimate WordPress API calls that the admin never explicitly approved.

WordPress's advisory notes that this escalation requires social engineering and explicit victim interaction, which is why the CVE carries a CVSS score of 8.9 rather than the maximum 10.0. The full chain was reproduced using pwn.ai's multi-agent AI workflow, building on a 2022 Same Origin Method Execution technique published by researcher Paulos Yibelo that was nominated for Top Web Hacking Technique of the year.

Patch and Response

WordPress shipped an emergency fix in version 7.0.3 on August 6, 2026, alongside eleven other security patches. The fix was backported to every maintained branch going back to WordPress 4.7. Most managed hosting providers apply updates automatically, but self-hosted sites often require manual intervention.

There is currently no evidence of active in-the-wild exploitation or a public proof-of-concept exploit, according to vulnerability trackers monitoring the CVE. However, the sheer scale of the vulnerable surface — WordPress powers more than 43% of all websites on the internet — means the risk remains significant.

XSS2Shell is separate from WP2Shell, another critical WordPress vulnerability chain (CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030) disclosed in July 2026 by Searchlight Cyber, which involved a REST API batch-route confusion and SQL injection chain. That vulnerability has seen active exploitation in the wild. Together, the two disclosures within weeks of each other underscore the ongoing security challenges facing the world's most widely deployed content management system.
nri_angle: Millions of Indian businesses and developers rely on WordPress for their websites, making this critical vulnerability directly relevant to the Indian tech community
